label: Animal parts are either uniform (homogeneous) or composite
claim: The parts of animals are of two kinds: simple parts, which divide into parts like themselves (as flesh into flesh), and composite parts, which do not (a hand does not divide into hands).
quote: Of the parts of animals some are simple: to wit, all such as divide into parts uniform with themselves, as flesh into flesh; others are composite, such as divide into parts not uniform with themselves
candidate_data: none known

label: Parts of different genera can correspond only by analogy, as feather to scale
claim: Animals of different genera may have parts that are the same only by analogy: bone corresponds to fish-bone, nail to hoof, hand to claw, and the feather of a bird to the scale of a fish.
quote: they are the same only in the way of analogy, as, for instance, bone is only analogous to fish-bone, nail to hoof, hand to claw, and scale to feather; for what the feather is in a bird, the scale is in a fish.
scope: Animals of different genera, e.g. birds and fishes
measurable_quantities: correspondence of integumentary and skeletal structures across taxa
candidate_data: Anatomy ontologies such as Uberon and the Phenoscape Knowledgebase, which record homology and analogy relations between structures.

label: The gadfly develops from river worms that leave the water
claim: Some animals live first in water and later change their shape and live out of water; the gadfly develops from river worms in this way.
quote: Some animals at first live in water, and by and by change their shape and live out of water, as is the case with river worms, for out of these the gadfly develops.
scope: Insects with aquatic larvae; the 'gadfly' (oistros, an insect of uncertain identity)
measurable_quantities: larval habitat (aquatic vs terrestrial) of the species identified as the gadfly
occurrence of metamorphosis from aquatic larva to aerial adult
candidate_data: Insect life-history and larval-habitat records such as the freshwater ecology trait databases and the Animal Diversity Web.

label: No bird with crooked talons is gregarious
claim: No bird with crooked talons (a bird of prey) lives in flocks.
quote: no bird furnished with crooked talons is gregarious
scope: Birds with hooked talons (raptors: eagles, hawks, falcons, owls, vultures)
measurable_quantities: flocking or colonial behaviour across raptor species
candidate_data: AVONET and the Birds of the World species accounts for social and flocking behaviour; EltonTraits for diet to define raptors.

label: Every domesticated kind of animal also exists in a wild form
claim: Whenever a kind of animal is found domesticated, the same kind is always also found wild, as with horses, cattle, swine, sheep, goats and dogs.
quote: whenever a race of animals is found domesticated, the same is always to be found in a wild condition; as we find to be the case with horses, kine, swine, (men), sheep, goats, and dogs.
scope: Domesticated animals: horse, cattle, pig, sheep, goat, dog (and, in the translator's bracket, man)
measurable_quantities: existence of extant wild or feral populations for each domesticated species
candidate_data: IUCN Red List status of wild progenitors and GBIF occurrence records of wild and feral populations of domestic species.

label: An animal with a bladder always has an intestine, but not conversely
claim: Every animal that has a bladder for wet residue also has an intestine for dry residue, but an animal may have an intestine without a bladder.
quote: In other words, an animal has a bowel or intestine if it have a bladder; but an animal may have a bowel and be without a bladder.
scope: All animals with organs for excreting residue
measurable_quantities: presence of a urinary bladder
presence of an intestine
candidate_data: Comparative anatomy compiled in Uberon and the Phenoscape Knowledgebase for presence/absence of urinary bladder and intestine across taxa.

label: Touch is the only sense common to all animals
claim: Touch is the one and only sense that all animals possess.
quote: One sense, and one alone, is common to all animals-the sense of touch.
measurable_quantities: presence of mechanosensory capacity across animal phyla
presence of other senses (vision, chemoreception, hearing) across phyla
candidate_data: Comparative sensory biology literature and Animal Diversity Web phylum accounts; no single dataset known.

label: Animals with more than four feet are bloodless
claim: All animals with more than four feet are bloodless, as are the bee, the wasp, the cuttlefish and the crawfish, while animals with blood have no feet, two feet or four feet.
quote: other animals are bloodless, such as the bee and the wasp, and, of marine animals, the cuttle-fish, the crawfish, and all such animals as have more than four feet.
scope: All footed animals; 'bloodless' roughly the invertebrates, 'blooded' roughly the vertebrates
measurable_quantities: number of legs
presence of red blood (vertebrate-type blood)
candidate_data: Open Tree of Life for vertebrate/invertebrate membership and Phenoscape or Uberon for limb counts.

label: In an egg the embryo forms from part of it, the rest being food
claim: In an egg the embryo arises from only part of the egg, and the rest serves as food for the developing embryo, whereas a grub develops into the animal as a whole.
quote: in respect to its primitive germ it comes from part only of the egg, while the rest serves for food as the germ develops.
scope: Oviparous animals (eggs) contrasted with grub-bearing animals (insects)
measurable_quantities: fraction of egg contents incorporated into embryo vs consumed as yolk
candidate_data: Developmental biology literature on yolk use in bird and reptile eggs; no single dataset known.

label: Sharks hatch eggs inside their own bodies
claim: Some viviparous animals, such as the sharks, hatch eggs inside their own bodies, while others, such as man and the horse, carry a live foetus.
quote: Of viviparous animals, some hatch eggs in their own interior, as creatures of the shark kind; others engender in their interior a live foetus, as man and the horse.
scope: Selachians (cartilaginous fishes) of the shark kind; viviparous mammals
measurable_quantities: reproductive mode (oviparity, yolk-sac viviparity/ovoviviparity, placental viviparity) across shark species
candidate_data: FishBase reproductive-guild fields and published compilations of chondrichthyan reproductive modes.

label: Bloodless animals are largest in mild climates and in the sea
claim: Among bloodless animals, the largest kinds live in milder climates, and those living in the sea are larger than those living on land or in fresh water.
quote: And of these bloodless genera, those are the largest that dwell in milder climates, and those that inhabit the sea are larger than those living on dry land or in fresh water.
measurable_quantities: maximum body size of invertebrate taxa by latitude/climate
maximum body size by habitat (marine, terrestrial, freshwater)
candidate_data: SeaLifeBase body sizes for marine invertebrates, GBIF occurrences for climate of range, and published invertebrate body-size compilations.

label: All hair-coated animals are viviparous
claim: Every animal with a coat of hair (counting the spines of hedgehogs and porcupines as hair) bears live young.
quote: All animals, however, that are hair-coated are viviparous.
measurable_quantities: reproductive mode across hair-bearing species, including monotremes
candidate_data: The Amniote Life-History Database and AnAge for reproductive mode across mammals.

label: Women's skulls have one circular suture, men's usually three meeting
claim: The skull of a woman has one circular suture, while the skull of a man, as a general rule, has three sutures meeting at a point.
quote: The skull has sutures: one, of circular form, in the case of women; in the case of men, as a general rule, three meeting at a point.
measurable_quantities: number and configuration of cranial sutures in male and female skulls
candidate_data: Human cranial CT and osteological collections such as those shared on MorphoSource.

label: The mole has stunted eyes hidden under the skin
claim: The mole cannot see and has no externally visible eyes, but beneath its skin lie the eye region and the dark parts of the eyes, stunted and overgrown by skin; it is the only viviparous animal without eyes.
quote: For in point of absolute fact it cannot see, and has no eyes visible externally; but when the outer skin is removed, it is found to have the place where eyes are usually situated, and the black parts of the eyes rightly situated
scope: The mole (Mediterranean moles, Talpa, or possibly mole-rats, Spalax)
measurable_quantities: presence and size of eyes beneath the skin
light perception or visual function
candidate_data: Specimen CT scans on MorphoSource and anatomical studies of eye reduction in Talpa and Spalax.

label: Man is the only, or nearly only, animal with varied eye colours
claim: Man is the only, or nearly the only, animal whose eyes vary in colour between individuals; other animals as a rule have eyes of a single colour, though some horses have blue eyes.
quote: Man is the only, or nearly the only, creature, that has eyes of diverse colours. Animals, as a rule, have eyes of one colour only.
scope: Man compared with other animals; horses as an exception
measurable_quantities: within-species variation in iris colour across species
candidate_data: Comparative iris-colour surveys of mammals and birds in the literature; no single dataset known.

label: The inner ear connects to the palate, not to the brain
claim: The inner cavity of the ear has no passage to the brain but does have a passage to the palate.
quote: This receptacle does not communicate by any passage with the brain, but does so with the palate
measurable_quantities: presence of a canal from middle ear to pharynx (auditory tube)
presence of an open passage from ear to brain cavity
candidate_data: Human and comparative anatomy in Uberon and the Foundational Model of Anatomy.

label: Man is the only animal with ears that cannot move them
claim: Of all animals that have ears, man is the only one that cannot move them.
quote: Of animals possessed of ears man is the only one that cannot move this organ.
measurable_quantities: capacity for voluntary pinna movement across mammal species, including apes
candidate_data: Comparative studies of auricular musculature in primates and other mammals; no single dataset known.

label: The crocodile alone moves its upper jaw instead of its lower
claim: All animals move the lower jaw except the river crocodile, which moves only its upper jaw.
quote: All animals move the lower jaw, with the exception of the river crocodile; this creature moves the upper jaw only.
scope: Animals with jaws; the Nile crocodile
measurable_quantities: relative motion of upper jaw (skull) and lower jaw during jaw opening in crocodiles
candidate_data: Published biomechanics and video kinematics of crocodylian feeding; no single dataset known.

label: Man has eight ribs on each side
claim: The human trunk has eight ribs on each side.
quote: Common to the upper and lower part of the trunk are the 'ribs', eight on either side
measurable_quantities: number of ribs per side in humans
candidate_data: Standard human anatomy and skeletal datasets, e.g. the Foundational Model of Anatomy and human CT collections on MorphoSource.

label: Man has the largest and moistest brain for his size
claim: Relative to body size, man has the largest and the moistest brain of any animal.
quote: But, taking size for size of animal, the largest brain, and the moistest, is that of man.
scope: Man compared with all other animals that have a brain
measurable_quantities: brain mass relative to body mass across species
brain water content
candidate_data: Comparative brain- and body-mass compilations for mammals and birds, and AnAge for body mass.

label: The brain is bloodless, has no veins and is cold
claim: In all animals the brain is bloodless, has no veins in it and is naturally cold to the touch.
quote: The brain in all animals is bloodless, devoid of veins, and naturally cold to the touch
measurable_quantities: blood perfusion and vascular density of brain tissue
brain temperature relative to body
candidate_data: Cerebral blood-flow and brain-temperature measurements in the physiology literature; Allen Brain Atlas vasculature data.

label: The heart has three cavities, the right largest and the left smallest
claim: The heart has three cavities: the right-hand one is the largest, the left-hand one the smallest, and the middle one intermediate in size.
quote: It has three cavities, as has been said: the right-hand one the largest of the three, the left-hand one the least, and the middle one intermediate in size.
scope: Man and the larger blooded animals
measurable_quantities: number of heart chambers
relative chamber volumes
candidate_data: Comparative cardiac anatomy in Uberon and human cardiac imaging data.

label: The lung is the organ most richly supplied with blood
claim: In animals that have a lung and bear live young, the lung is the organ most richly supplied with blood, being spongy and reached at every pore by branches of the great vein; it is not empty, as some suppose.
quote: the lung is of all organs the most richly supplied with blood; for the lung is throughout spongy in texture, and along by every single pore in it go branches from the great vein.
scope: Animals with lungs that are viviparous (mammals)
measurable_quantities: blood volume or blood flow per gram of tissue by organ
candidate_data: Organ blood-flow and blood-volume tables in mammalian physiology references.

label: The right kidney lies higher than the left in all animals
claim: In all animals that have kidneys, the right kidney lies higher in the body than the left.
quote: In all animals that are provided with this organ, the right kidney is situated higher up than the other.
measurable_quantities: relative craniocaudal position of right and left kidneys across species
candidate_data: Veterinary and human anatomical imaging; comparative anatomy references.

label: The lion's neck is a single bone without vertebrae
claim: The lion's neck consists of a single bone instead of vertebrae.
quote: The lion has its neck composed of one single bone instead of vertebrae
measurable_quantities: number of separate cervical vertebrae in the lion
candidate_data: Lion skeletal specimens and CT scans on MorphoSource; mammalian cervical vertebra counts in the literature.

label: The elephant sleeps lying on its side, not standing
claim: The elephant does not sleep standing; it bends its legs, settles down and sleeps lying on one side.
quote: The elephant does not sleep standing, as some were wont to assert, but it bends its legs and settles down
measurable_quantities: sleep posture (standing vs recumbent) in elephants
candidate_data: Published actigraphy and video studies of elephant sleep in the wild and in zoos.

label: Horned animals are mostly cloven-hoofed; none is solid-hoofed with two horns
claim: The great majority of horned animals are cloven-hoofed, and no solid-hoofed animal with a pair of horns has ever been found.
quote: The great majority of the horned animals are cloven-footed, as the ox, the stag, the goat; and a solid-hooved animal with a pair of horns has never yet been met with.
measurable_quantities: co-occurrence of paired horns or antlers with hoof type across ungulates
candidate_data: Phenoscape and PanTHERIA-style trait compilations of ungulate headgear and digit number; Open Tree of Life for taxon coverage.

label: Only the deer sheds its horns, annually after age two
claim: The deer is the only animal that sheds its horns; it does so every year after reaching the age of two and grows them again.
quote: The deer is the only animal that sheds its horns, and it does so annually, after reaching the age of two years, and again renews them.
scope: Deer and all other horned animals
measurable_quantities: annual shedding of headgear by species
age at first antler cast
candidate_data: Comparative literature on antler cycles in cervids and horn-sheath shedding in pronghorn; Animal Diversity Web accounts.

label: The fox, wolf, marten and weasel have a bony penis
claim: In some animals the penis is bony, as in the fox, the wolf, the marten and the weasel.
quote: in other cases it is bony, as with the fox, the wolf, the marten, and the weasel; for this organ in the weasel has a bone.
measurable_quantities: presence of a baculum (os penis)
candidate_data: Published comparative datasets on baculum presence across mammals; museum specimens on MorphoSource.

label: No animal has both tusks and horns, nor does any saw-toothed animal
claim: No animal has both tusks and horns, and no animal with interlocking pointed (saw-like) teeth has either tusks or horns.
quote: No animal is there that possesses both tusks and horns, nor yet do either of these structures exist in any animal possessed of 'saw-teeth'.
measurable_quantities: co-occurrence of tusks and horns/antlers across species
co-occurrence of carnassial or interlocking dentition with tusks or horns
candidate_data: Mammal trait compilations (PanTHERIA, Phenoscape) for headgear and dentition; Animal Diversity Web species accounts.

label: No animal sheds its molars, and the pig sheds no teeth at all
claim: Man sheds his front teeth, but no animal sheds its molars, and the pig sheds none of its teeth at all.
quote: And man sheds his front teeth; but there is no instance of an animal that sheds its molars. The pig sheds none of its teeth at all.
scope: Man and mammals with tooth replacement; the pig
measurable_quantities: replacement of deciduous cheek teeth by species
presence of tooth replacement in pigs
candidate_data: Mammalian dental eruption and replacement schedules in veterinary and comparative odontology references.

label: Teeth blacken with age except in the horse, whose teeth whiten
claim: As animals grow older their teeth generally become blacker, but the horse's teeth become whiter with age.
quote: for, generally speaking, as animals grow older their teeth get blacker, but the horse's teeth grow whiter with age.
measurable_quantities: tooth colour by age in horses and other mammals
candidate_data: Equine dental ageing guides and photographic datasets of tooth wear by age.

label: Males have more teeth than females in man, sheep, goats and swine
claim: In men, sheep, goats and swine, males have more teeth than females.
quote: Males have more teeth than females in the case of men, sheep, goats, and swine
measurable_quantities: adult tooth count by sex
candidate_data: Dental formulae in mammal anatomy references and the Animal Diversity Web; sex-specific dental records in veterinary literature.

label: Animals with more teeth live longer, as a rule
claim: As a rule, animals with more teeth live longer, and those with fewer and more thinly set teeth are correspondingly short-lived.
quote: the more teeth they have the more long-lived are they, as a rule, while those are short-lived in proportion that have teeth fewer in number and thinly set.
scope: Animals with teeth (men, sheep, goats, swine and others)
measurable_quantities: tooth count
maximum or mean lifespan
candidate_data: AnAge for maximum lifespan combined with dental formulae from mammal anatomy references; human longevity cohorts with dental counts.

label: Oviparous quadrupeds lack external ears, breasts and a copulatory organ
claim: Oviparous blooded quadrupeds have no external ears but only an auditory passage, no breasts, no copulatory organ, and no external testicles, only internal ones.
quote: Again, oviparous blooded quadrupeds are unprovided with ears, but possess only the passage for hearing; neither have they breasts, nor a copulatory organ, nor external testicles, but internal ones only
measurable_quantities: presence of external ear
presence of mammary glands
presence of intromittent organ (hemipenes, phallus)
testis position
candidate_data: Comparative reptile and amphibian anatomy in Phenoscape and Uberon; herpetological anatomy literature.

label: River crocodiles spend the day on land and the night in water
claim: As a rule, river crocodiles spend the daytime on land and the night in the water.
quote: As a rule, they pass the day-time on land and the nighttime in the water
measurable_quantities: proportion of time on land vs in water by time of day
candidate_data: Telemetry and temperature-logger studies of Nile crocodile thermoregulation; Movebank tracking data where available.

label: Crocodiles enter water at night because it is then warmer than the air
claim: Crocodiles spend the night in the water because at night the water is warmer than the open air.
quote: for the temperature of the water is at night-time more genial than that of the open air.
measurable_quantities: night-time water vs air temperature in crocodile habitats
crocodile body temperature by location at night
candidate_data: Thermoregulation studies of crocodylians with body-temperature loggers; meteorological and water-temperature records for their habitats.

label: The chameleon changes colour when it inflates itself with air
claim: The chameleon changes colour when it is inflated with air, turning black, or green with black spots, over its whole body including the eyes and tail.
quote: The change in its colour takes place when it is inflated with air; it is then black, not unlike the crocodile, or green like the lizard but black-spotted like the pard.
measurable_quantities: co-occurrence of body inflation and colour change
colour states displayed
candidate_data: Published behavioural and physiological studies of chameleon colour change; no single dataset known.

label: High-flying birds are four-toed, most three-forward one-back
claim: Birds that fly high are all four-toed; most have three toes in front and one behind, and a few, such as the wryneck, have two in front and two behind.
quote: Birds that fly high in air are in all cases four-toed: that is, the greater part have three toes in front and one behind in place of a heel; some few have two in front and two behind, as the wryneck.
scope: Birds that fly high; the wryneck (Jynx torquilla)
measurable_quantities: toe number
toe arrangement (anisodactyl, zygodactyl)
flight habit
candidate_data: AVONET morphological traits and published foot-type classifications of birds.

label: No fish has a neck, limbs, testicles or breasts
claim: No fish has a neck, any limb, testicles (internal or external), or breasts.
quote: No fish has a neck, or any limb, or testicles at all, within or without, or breasts.
measurable_quantities: presence of neck
presence of limbs
presence of testes
presence of mammary glands
candidate_data: FishBase and Phenoscape for fish anatomy, including gonad anatomy.

label: The dolphin has two breasts near its genitals
claim: The dolphin bears live young directly and has two breasts placed near its genitals rather than high up, with no visible teats but two slits from which milk flows.
quote: Thus the dolphin is directly viviparous, and accordingly we find it furnished with two breasts, not situated high up, but in the neighbourhood of the genitals.
measurable_quantities: number and position of mammary glands and slits
candidate_data: Cetacean anatomy literature and specimen records; Animal Diversity Web accounts.

label: Fishes have no organs or passages for hearing or smell
claim: Of the sense organs fishes have only eyes; they have neither the organs of hearing and smell nor any passages for them.
quote: with regard to the organs connected with the other senses, hearing and smell, they are devoid alike of the organs themselves and of passages indicative of them.
measurable_quantities: presence of inner ear
presence of nares and olfactory epithelium
candidate_data: Phenoscape and FishBase for fish sensory anatomy.

label: Scaly fish lay eggs; cartilaginous fish bear live young
claim: Scaly fishes are always oviparous, and cartilaginous fishes are all viviparous except the fishing-frog.
quote: scaly fish are invariably oviparous, but cartilaginous fishes are all viviparous, with the single exception of the fishing-frog.
scope: Scaly (bony) fishes and selachians (cartilaginous fishes); the fishing-frog (anglerfish, Lophius)
measurable_quantities: reproductive mode across scaly bony fishes and chondrichthyans
candidate_data: FishBase reproductive-guild fields for teleosts and chondrichthyans.

label: Some oxen and the horse have a bone inside the heart
claim: In one kind of ox, though not in every individual, a bone is found inside the heart, and the horse's heart also has a bone in it.
quote: there is one species of ox where, though not in all cases, a bone is found inside the heart. And, by the way, the horse's heart also has a bone inside it.
measurable_quantities: presence and prevalence of an os cordis (cardiac bone) in cattle and horses
candidate_data: Veterinary anatomy literature on the os cordis in ruminants and equids.

label: Deer, horse, mule, ass, seal and some pigs lack a gall-bladder
claim: Among viviparous quadrupeds the deer, the roe, the horse, the mule, the ass, the seal and some kinds of pig have no gall-bladder.
quote: Of viviparous quadrupeds the deer is without the organ, as also the roe, the horse, the mule, the ass, the seal, and some kinds of pigs.
scope: Deer, roe deer, horse, mule, ass, seal, pigs
measurable_quantities: presence of a gall-bladder by species
candidate_data: Comparative mammalian anatomy literature and Uberon/Phenoscape presence-absence records for the gall bladder.

label: Stags always have about twenty maggots inside the head
claim: Without exception, stags have maggots living inside the head, in the hollow beneath the root of the tongue and near the first vertebra, usually about twenty in a cluster.
quote: However, without any exception, stags are found to have maggots living inside the head
measurable_quantities: prevalence of nasopharyngeal larvae in deer
number of larvae per host
candidate_data: Parasitological surveys of deer nasal bot flies (Cephenemyia) and host-parasite databases.

label: No fish or bird has kidneys or a bladder
claim: No oviparous animal that is not a quadruped, whether fish or bird, is known to have kidneys or a bladder.
quote: Of the ovipara that are not quadrupedal there is no instance known of an animal, whether fish or bird, provided with these organs.
measurable_quantities: presence of kidneys
presence of urinary bladder
candidate_data: Comparative anatomy in Uberon and the Phenoscape Knowledgebase for kidney and bladder presence in fishes and birds.

label: Horned animals lacking upper front teeth have four stomachs and ruminate
claim: Horned quadrupeds that lack a full set of teeth in both jaws have a stomach of four chambers, and these are the animals that chew the cud.
quote: such of the horned animals as are not equally furnished with teeth in both jaws are furnished with four such chambers. These animals, by the way, are those that are said to chew the cud.
measurable_quantities: presence of upper incisors
number of stomach chambers
rumination
candidate_data: Comparative digestive anatomy literature and mammal trait compilations; Animal Diversity Web accounts.

label: Serpents have thirty ribs, as many as the days of a month
claim: Serpents have thirty ribs.
quote: Their ribs are as numerous as the days of the month; in other words, they are thirty in number.
measurable_quantities: number of rib pairs in snakes
candidate_data: Vertebral and rib counts for snakes in herpetological literature and CT scans on MorphoSource.
